newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farm output show healthy '96 growth.
newsitem.headline: French farm output show healthy '96 growth.

text.p: France's output of agricultural produce grew a healthy 2.4 percent last year, boosted by a strong rise in grain production, and the food industry output grew 1.8 percent, the National Statistics Institute INSEE said on Wednesday.
In its annual farm report, INSEE said the 1996 grain crop was up 13.7 percent, the biggest single-year increase in a decade.
Animal products were up 1.9 percent, with cattle up five percent despite the health scare due to mad cow disease.
But domestic beef consumption was down eight percent because of fears that Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) could spread to humans, pushing up meat stocks to 80,000 tonnes.
INSEE said French farm exports exceeded imports by 57.5 billion francs ($10 billion), up by six billion francs over the previous year.
Exports of grain, oilseeds and wine were up, while the cost of imports was cut by a fall in the prices of tropical products and a decrease in purchase of timber.
The surplus in the food industry reached a record 33 billion francs, mainly due to a fall in imports.
INSEE said the average income per farm grew by one percent, mainly because of a continuing trend towards cutting the number of farms and increasing their average size. ($ = 5.823 French Francs)
